Use the pinned @babylonjs/havok browser loader and a browser event-loop yield; keep Node imports out of the browser entry.
Make runtime-init failure explicit and typed; do not silently fall back to a mock or NullEngine.
Preserve existing scene, mesh and type exports; do not expose scheduling internals on the wire.
The later T02-R05 Chromium test must prove this factory actually initializes WASM and moves bodies.

checks.command: pnpm --filter @korre/counterball typecheck && pnpm verify
checks.expected: Browser entry compiles with real WASM loader and no Node-only imports.

checks.command: Independent source review of pinned browser loader and export surface
checks.expected: Export matches C00 contract and same runner; no mock or duplicate implementation.

acceptance: Browser consumer can import the canonical runner factory from @korre/counterball/browser.
Actual runtime proof is reserved for T02-R05; this export packet does not claim physics execution by itself.
negative_cases: NullEngine/Node fallback, duplicate browser-only physics code, DOM types in protocol or loader failure treated as success.
review_questions: Is the pinned WASM package imported through supported browser entry?
Does the factory invoke the exact canonical runner?
Are existing browser exports preserved?
stop_conditions: If bundling/runtime loader cannot run in Chromium, stop and report the exact blocker; do not use a mock.
